haiku-low.q1: Step 4, after step 3 passes and before any new-release instance exists. The live colour (old release) must still work, since migrations are additive.
haiku-low.q2: Only in a later release, after the release still using the old column or table has been retired (step 11 of the deploy that replaced it).
haiku-low.q3: All 4 instances must pass 3 consecutive /healthz checks, then smoke tests must pass, before gate_deadline (10 minutes). Otherwise Abort.
haiku-low.q4: Step 8 repoints the public listener from the old target group to the new one in one change. New requests go to the new colour; in-flight requests finish on the old.
haiku-low.q5: A 5xx rate above 1% over a rolling 5-minute window, from T to T+15 min. Rollback repoints the listener to the old colour and scales the new colour to 0. It never reverses migrations.
haiku-low.q6: Until step 11 at T+30, when the old colour is scaled to 0. An engineer starts the rollback job for problems found. After that, rollback means a normal deploy of the previous release.
haiku-low.q7: A failed transaction rolls back, leaving the schema unchanged. A failed index build drops the invalid index; additive changes stay. The run stops, the new colour never starts, and the run fails.
haiku-low.q8: Step 2 reads which target group the public listener forwards to; that colour is live. The listener is the lasting record; run variables live_colour and new_colour hold the values for the run.
haiku-low.q9: A CI concurrency group, such as deploy-catalog-web; later runs queue. A run holds it from step 1 until step 12 finishes.
haiku-low.q10: Step 5 points the internal test listener, reachable only from CI, at the new target group. The smoke suite runs through it while users stay on the live colour.
haiku-low.q11: The pipeline runs one migrate task from the new image at step 4. Instances never migrate on startup, so migrations run exactly once per deploy.
haiku-low.q12: Its instances are scaled to 0, leaving it idle and empty. The next deploy's step 2 scales it to 0 first if any instances remain, then deploys into it.

sonnet.q1: Step 4, after build/check (step 3) and before any new-colour instance starts. The live (old) colour must keep working on the migrated schema (migrations are additive).
sonnet.q2: Only in a later release, after the release that still used the old column/table has been retired (in step 11 of the deploy that replaced it).
sonnet.q3: All 4 new instances must pass 3 consecutive /healthz checks (checked every 10s), then the smoke suite must pass via the test listener, all before gate_deadline (step 5 time + 10 min). If not in time, Abort: scale new colour to 0, leave the public listener alone, go to step 12 (failed).
sonnet.q4: In step 8, the public listener is repointed from the old target group to the new one in a single change; new requests go to the new colour, and the old colour keeps running so in-flight requests finish.
sonnet.q5: Automatic: the public listener's 5xx rate (rolling 5-minute window) going above 1% during T to T+15 min (an engineer can also start the rollback job manually). Rollback repoints the listener to the old colour's target group, scales the new colour to 0 and alerts the team. It never reverses migrations (they stay applied).
sonnet.q6: Until step 11 at T+30 min (old colour stays running until then). After that there is no fast switch back; the fix is a normal deploy of the previous release through this checklist.
sonnet.q7: If the table/column transaction fails, it rolls back and the schema is unchanged. If an index build fails, the invalid index is dropped; committed table/column changes stay and the unrecorded index migration reruns next deploy. Either way the deploy stops: new colour never started, live colour keeps serving, go to step 12 (failed).
sonnet.q8: Step 2 reads which target group the public listener forwards to; that colour is live and the other is new. The listener is the only lasting record (no state file); the run writes live_colour and new_colour to pipeline run variables, discarded when the run ends.
sonnet.q9: A CI concurrency group (e.g. deploy-catalog-web); one run holds it and later runs queue. The run keeps it from step 1 until step 12 (released then, or by CI if the run dies).
sonnet.q10: Via the internal test listener (reachable only from CI, e.g. port 8443) pointed at the new colour's target group; the public listener stays on the live colour.
sonnet.q11: One `migrate` task run by the pipeline from the new image against the shared database (step 4). Instances never migrate on startup, so migrations run exactly once per deploy.
sonnet.q12: Both scale the new colour to 0 (idle and empty). If the scale-down fails the team is alerted, and step 2 of the next deploy scales that colour to 0 before using it.
